---
title: "Run GWAS for SNP or Microhaplotype Markers"
---

## Run GWAS for SNP or Microhaplotype Markers {.unnumbered}


### Description

Performs genome-wide association study (GWAS) for SNP or microhaplotype
(MH) markers. Uses EMMAX (Efficient Mixed-Model Association eXpedited)
to control for population structure and relatedness, preventing spurious
associations. Results can be inspected for QTL detection or passed
directly to <code>gwablup()</code> for GWAS-assisted genomic prediction.



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>run_gwas(
  markers,
  y,
  masreml_fit,
  X = NULL,
  pi = 0.001,
  window = 5L,
  ref_markers = NULL
)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="markers">markers</code></td>
<td>
list of raw marker inputs. Provide one of:


<ul>
<li> <code>snp_add</code>: numeric matrix (n x m), genotype coded 0/1/2

</li>
<li> <code>mh_add</code>: list of data.frames, one per chromosome,
with paired haplotype columns per block

</li></ul>
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="y">y</code></td>
<td>
numeric named vector of phenotypes (length n). Names must
match row names of marker matrix.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="masreml_fit">masreml_fit</code></td>
<td>
fitted <code>masreml</code> object from <code>masreml()</code>.
Used to account for population structure in the GWAS model.
Must be fitted with the same markers and individuals.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="X">X</code></td>
<td>
fixed effects design matrix (n x c). If NULL, intercept only.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="pi">pi</code></td>
<td>
numeric, prior probability that a marker has a non-zero
effect (default 0.001). Lower values make posterior probabilities
more conservative.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="window">window</code></td>
<td>
integer, number of adjacent markers used in moving
average smoothing of likelihood ratios (default 5). Larger values
produce smoother posterior probabilities.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="ref_markers">ref_markers</code></td>
<td>
list of raw marker data for training individuals only,
in the same format as <code>markers</code>. If provided, allele frequencies
for building G_u (used in EMMAX) are computed from <code>ref_markers</code>
instead of <code>markers</code>. Use this when running GWAS in a train/test
context to avoid data leakage from test individuals into the
population structure correction matrix.
Supported elements: <code>snp_add</code> (matrix) or <code>mh_add</code> (list).
If NULL (default), allele frequencies are computed from <code>markers</code>.
</td></tr>
</table>


### Value

Object of class <code>"gwas_result"</code> with elements:


<ul>
<li> <code>lr</code>: log-likelihood ratio per marker/block

</li>
<li> <code>beta</code>: effect estimate per marker/block

</li>
<li> <code>se</code>: standard error per marker/block

</li>
<li> <code>pval</code>: p-value per marker/block

</li>
<li> <code>smoothed_lr</code>: smoothed LR after moving average

</li>
<li> <code>pp</code>: posterior probability of non-zero effect per
marker/block — use this as input to <code>gwablup()</code>

</li>
<li> <code>marker_type</code>: <code>"snp"</code> or <code>"mh"</code>

</li>
<li> <code>n_markers</code>: number of markers or MH blocks

</li>
<li> <code>pi</code>: prior probability used

</li>
<li> <code>window</code>: smoothing window size used

</li></ul>



### References

Kang et al. (2010) Variance component model to account for
sample structure in GWAS. <em>Nat Genet.</em> 42:348-354.

Meuwissen et al. (2024) GWABLUP: genome-wide association
assisted BLUP. <em>Genet Sel Evol.</em> 56:17.



### See Also

<code>masreml</code>, <code>gwablup</code>



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=FALSE}
library("masreml")

# ── Standard workflow (all individuals) ───────────────────
# Step 1: fit standard GBLUP
fit <- masreml(y, markers = list(snp_add = W))

# Step 2: run GWAS — inspect QTL signals
gwas <- run_gwas(
  markers     = list(snp_add = W),
  y           = y,
  masreml_fit = fit
)
summary(gwas)

# Step 3: run GWABLUP using GWAS weights
fit_wa <- gwablup(y, markers = list(snp_add = W), gwas_result = gwas)
summary(fit_wa)

# ── Train/test workflow (no data leakage) ─────────────────
# Step 1: fit GBLUP on training only
fit_tr <- masreml(y_train, markers = list(snp_add = W_train))

# Step 2: run GWAS on training — ref_markers = training markers
gwas_tr <- run_gwas(
  markers     = list(snp_add = W_train),
  y           = y_train,
  masreml_fit = fit_tr,
  ref_markers = list(snp_add = W_train)
)

# Step 3: GWABLUP on training with training-based freq
fit_wa_tr <- gwablup(
  y           = y_train,
  markers     = list(snp_add = W_train),
  gwas_result = gwas_tr,
  ref_markers = list(snp_add = W_train)
)

# Step 4: predict test set
G_full <- build_G_snp(W_all, ref_W = W_train)
pred   <- predict(fit_wa_tr,
                  G_full    = list(snp_add = G_full),
                  train_ids = rownames(W_train),
                  test_ids  = rownames(W_test))




```
